statements.quote: 480 screened-in participants (160 per language group) were taken to one of three surveys on Qualtrics. The English survey is provided in Section B1. Section B1.1 provides screenshots of how the survey appeared in three languages. Participants were first required to read the consent form and provide informed consent before proceeding to the next section. Then, participants answered an attention check question on the payment scheme (consent form available upon request). The study included those who failed the attention check questions in the 480-participant sample, but excluded them during the analysis. Next, participants were asked to complete an email-writing task (more information in the next section). This is the core part of the survey. Subsequently, participants would answer questions on how often they use AI tools in work or life, how difficult they found the email-writing task, and how confident they were about the quality of their email. Then, they were asked to write two to sentences about how they felt about the task. Finally, they were directed back to the platform for payment.

deposits.notes: The publisher supplement is cited on PDF p. 10. GET https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-16650-w redirected to https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-16650-w; both returned HTTP 200 with title Client Challenge instead of article content. No challenge was bypassed. Independent public mirror https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12373962/fullTextXML returned HTTP 200 and identified this DOCX as Supplementary Material 1 (two XML references to the same file, counted once). The public S3 list endpoint https://pmc-oa-opendata.s3.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2&prefix=PMC12373962.1/ returned HTTP 200 and confirmed the filename and size; the other objects are article formats, metadata, and figures, not additional data files. The DOCX was downloaded and read entirely in memory. It contains methods, preregistration text, materials, aggregate tables S1-S13, and figures S1-S7. No embedded spreadsheet or chart-data members were present in its DOCX archive. B3.5 prints exactly three example participant emails: English R&D with AI treatment, Arabic Marketing without AI treatment, and Chinese Customer Service without AI treatment. These have scenario/condition labels but no participant IDs or linked outcome ratings and do not form an analysis dataset. Hence has_texts_or_ideas=true applies only to these examples; has_arm_assignment=false and has_outcome_scores=false mean no participant-level assignment/score data were available. rows_checked and columns_checked are null because no participant/output data table was inspected. A1.5 explicitly averages the two evaluator ratings for each email and dimension. Table S3 headings report Control (N=235) and Treatment (N=224); Table S4 reports English (N=153), Arabic (N=123), and Chinese (N=147). These totals disagree; S5 and S9 do not supply analysis observation counts. Thus the final analyzed total and language-by-arm counts cannot be verified from these tables alone. A1.3 says attention-check failures are included in the 480-participant sample but excluded from analysis. B3.1 gives email-evaluator backgrounds; B4.1 concerns AI-content evaluators, contrary to the screening form's provisional locator for S2. The main article declares CC BY 4.0, but no file-specific license statement was confirmed for this DOCX, so license is null.

what_we_could_compute: Quality-effect extraction for S2-O1 through S2-O4: Table S5 provides aggregate regression coefficients and participant-clustered standard errors. Under the unadjusted AI-by-language specification printed on PDF p. 3, its rounded coefficients permit reconstruction of approximate fitted quality means for the six language-by-arm cells and language-specific AI-minus-control point estimates. They do not provide per-person records, arm SDs, all arm-mean SEs, the coefficient covariance matrix, or the standardizing SD.

Email-length extraction for S2-O5: Table S9 provides language-specific AI treatment effects and their reported clustered standard errors, control intercepts, and the character-normalization procedure. Approximate treatment-arm means can be derived by adding the within-language intercept and treatment coefficient. Complete per-person means/distributions, arm SDs, and full uncertainty cannot be independently recomputed.

No confirmed public dataset supports recomputing the final analyzed participant counts after all exclusions, the language-by-arm analyzed counts, or representative diversity/homogenization measures. The three example emails are insufficient. Other open items can be informed directly by the public documents: rating averaging in SI A1.5, recruitment/setting in A1.1-A1.3, evaluator backgrounds in B3.1, scale anchors in B3.2, normalization in Table S9, and primary outcomes in OSF registration response q15.question.
notes: The complete local markdown conversion was read (all 306 lines, including references and end matter); relevant quotations were checked against the local ten-page PDF with PyMuPDF. The separately hosted Supplementary Information DOCX was also read through its references, entirely in memory. Quotes preserve wording; PDF line breaks/whitespace and invisible URL typesetting were normalized. The main PDF has no appended supplement and no separate code-availability statement. public_partial reflects verified public aggregate tables, materials, and three illustrative participant emails; it does not establish public availability of the analysis dataset. The main Figshare data link remains unverified because it returned HTTP 202 with no content. No participant-level columns or rows were available to inspect, so public_participant_data would be unsupported. Both OSF records are public descriptions/preregistration only, with zero files. Consent forms and additional scenario texts are explicitly available upon request in the SI; this is a materials request, not a statement that the evaluation dataset is available on request. API searches used Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no login or personal identifier. Search queries and returned counts (including failed/capped searches) are recorded above; repeated identical requests are consolidated. The additional links quoted on PDF p. 10 were checked: https://www.nature.com/reprints returned HTTP 200 with a Client Challenge, and http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ returned HTTP 200 after redirecting to its HTTPS license page. The form's code_url is empty. No credentials, access request, CAPTCHA solution, or bot-check workaround was used. Only forms/data/c414.json was written.
